summary: Mipam Chökyi Jampa studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Mipham Chokyi Lodro (1952–2014) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Kalu Rinpoche (1973), and taught Trinley Thaye Dorje and Ole Nydahl.

Working in Buddhist studies and religious studies, Miranda Shaw studied under doctoral supervisor Masatoshi Nagatomi (attested 1994), Robert A. F. Thurman, and postdoctoral mentor Bratindra Nath Mukherjee.

Mircea Eliade (1907–1986) worked in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned a PhD at the University of Bucharest under Nae Ionescu, studied at the University of Calcutta under Surendranath Dasgupta, and later served as professor at the University of Chicago.
Mireille Helffer (1928–2023) worked in Tibetology. She served as Chargé de Recherche at the CNRS (~1961–1993) and held a post at Paris Nanterre University (attested 1985).

Miri Albahari works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She earned an MA at the University of Otago and a PhD at the University of Calgary under John A. Baker, later holding posts at the University of Western Australia and UNSW.

Miriam Levering (1943–2017) specialized in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. She earned her PhD from Harvard University in 1978 and served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Tennessee (attested 2007–2010).

Mirjan Damaška (1931–2023) studied at the University of Zagreb, the Hague Academy, and the University of Ljubljana (PhD). He held posts at the University of Zagreb, the University of Pennsylvania, and Yale Law School (~1976–2023).

Mirle Srinivasa Nagaraja Rao (1932–2011) was an Indologist and archaeologist. Educated at the University of Mysore and Pune University under M. N. Deshpande, he held posts at Karnatak University and was Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1984–1987).
Mitchell G. Weiss works in Indology. He studied under Ludo Rocher and held a post as professor at the University of Basel.

Mitsuji Fukunaga (1918–2001) was a scholar of philosophy, sinology, and religious studies. Educated at Kyoto University, he later served as professor at Kyoto University (1961–1982), the University of Tokyo (1974–1979), Kansai University, and the University of Kitakyushu.
Mitsukuni Yoshida (1921–1991) worked in Japanology and history and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1942–1945) and held a post at Kyoto University of the Arts.
Mitsutoshi Moriguchi (b. 1944) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he also served as a lecturer (attested 1989–1995).

Mitsuyoshi Saegusa (1923–2010) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo, the University of Munich, and Kokugakuin University, later holding professorships at the University of Tsukuba and Nihon University.

Mitsuyuki Ishida (1911–1991) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Ryukoku University (~1930–1934), where he later served as professor (~1950–1976), and was also a professor at International Buddhist University (attested 1976).
Miyoko Nakano (b. 1933) is a sinologist. She studied at Hokkaido University from ~1952 to 1956 and later held a post there from ~1970 to 1996.

Mizuho Okita (b. 1977) works in Indology and religious studies. She studied at Tokai University and Gakushuin University under Katsuhiko Kamimura and Atsuhiko Yoshida, and held a part-time lecturing post at Meisei University (attested 2008).
Mizumaro Ishida (1917–2004) was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Tokai University (attested 1976 and 1987).
Mohammad Ashraf Dar is an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar who completed a Master of Philosophy and worked as a research scholar at Vikram University (attested 2014).
Mohammad Habib (1895–1971) was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at Aligarh Muslim University (~1912–1916), the University of Allahabad (~1916–1918), and New College (~1919–1922).
